You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

In your continual harness, entries created without global_=True belong to this session and are lost with it.

This looks like a known ARC pattern: a small "key" pattern embedded in a solid background. Let me check memories? Probably request a demo first. Small pattern at rows 3-5, cols 1-3: cells: (3,0)=7,(3,3)=3,(4,1)=7,(4,2)=3,(5,1)=4,(5,2)=3. Hmm. Likely the output is a tiled pattern? Request a demo to be safe.

Non-bg pixels: 7 at (0,0), 7 at (1,1), 3 at (0,3),(1,2),(2,2), 4 at (2,1). Pattern in 3x4 box. Unknown output — likely repeat/tile the pattern across the grid. I should request a demo to learn the rule.

Demo: input has pattern: 3 at (0,3), 3 at (1,4), 0 at (1,5), 7 at (2,4), 2 at (2,5), 7 at (3,3). Output adds: 7 at (4,2), (5,1), (6,0). So a "7" diagonal continues: 7 appears at (2,4),(3,3) and output extends diagonal down-left: (4,2),(5,1),(6,0). Direction: down-left (down 1, left 1)? From (3,3): (4,2),(5,1),(6,0) yes.

Also 2 at (2,5), 0 at (1,5) unchanged. Hmm, which colors extend? The 7 diagonal. Also maybe 3 diagonal: 3 at (0,3),(1,4) — extends down-right? (2,5)? that's 2... hmm 2 at (2,5) maybe should become 3? No, output unchanged. So 3 diagonal... 3 at (0,3),(1,4), next would be (2,5) but there is 2. Hmm.

Wait maybe rule: extend each colored diagonal until hitting the edge, but only some color? 7 extends down-left. 3 diagonal at (0,3),(1,4) then (2,5) occupied by 2 — so stopped? And 2 and 0 are single pixels, not extended? Maybe rule: lines (diagonals) get extended to grid edge, but 2 and 0 are dots not lines. 7 is a line (2 cells) extended. 3 is a line (2 cells) but next cell (2,5) is occupied by 2 — blocked, so nothing added. That fits.

Now test input: pixels: 7 at (3,0); 7 at (4,1); 3 at (3,3),(4,2); 4 at (5,1); 3 at (5,2).

Diagonals: 7: (3,0) single; (4,1) single — antidiagonal? (3,0) and (4,1) is down-right diagonal but offset. Hmm. 3: (3,3),(4,2) down-left diagonal, and (5,2) single. 4: (5,1) single.

In demo, 7 diagonal (2,4),(3,3) is down-left; extended further down-left. 3 diagonal (0,3),(1,4) is down-right; blocked.

Test: 3 diagonal (3,3),(4,2) down-left, extend: (5,1) occupied by 4 — blocked. Also 7's: (3,0),(4,1) is down-right diagonal of 7! Extend: (5,2) occupied by 3 — blocked. Hmm then nothing extends? But (5,2) is 3... hmm but 3 at (5,2) plus? 3 pixels: (3,3),(4,2) diag down-left; (5,2) separate.

Maybe colors matter: maybe only 7 extends. In demo, 7 extended. In test, 7s: (3,0) and (4,1). Extend 7 down-right from (4,1): (5,2) is 3 — blocked. Extend down-left from (3,0): (4,-1) off grid. So maybe nothing? That seems unlikely.

Alternative: maybe all colored diagonals extend but overwrite non-background only? Or extend through? Let's think: perhaps extension goes until edge, overwriting? In demo output, (2,5) stays 2, so no overwrite.

Alternatively the direction: lines continue in their direction to the edge but blocked by any other color. Then in test: 7 diag (3,0),(4,1) direction down-right, next (5,2)=3 blocked. 3 diag (3,3),(4,2) direction down-left, next (5,1)=4 blocked. 3 at (5,2): single cell, no direction? A single cell — no line. 4 at (5,1): single. 7 at (3,0) belongs to the 7 line. So output = input unchanged? Suspicious.

Hmm, maybe lines extend in BOTH directions? 7 line (3,0),(4,1): other direction up-left — off grid. 3 line (3,3),(4,2): other direction up-right: (2,4). Add 3 at (2,4)! And continue: (1,5),(0,6). In demo, 3 line (0,3),(1,4): other direction up-left off grid; down-right blocked by 2. 7 line (2,4),(3,3): other direction up-right: (1,5)=0 — blocked. So blocking by non-bg... but demo output (1,5) stays 0. Consistent.

But singles: 4 at (5,1), 3 at (5,2), 0 at (1,5), 2 at (2,5) — singles not extended in demo (0 and 2 unchanged). So rule: each maximal diagonal of length≥2 of same color extends in both directions along the diagonal until edge or blocked by a non-background pixel.

- 7 diag (3,0),(4,1): extend up-left off grid; down-right next (5,2)=3 blocked.
- 3 diag (3,3),(4,2): extend up-right: (2,4),(1,5),(0,6) all bg → add 3s. Down-left: (5,1)=4 blocked.
- Any other length-2 same-color diagonals? 3 at (5,2) with 3 at (4,2)? vertical, not diagonal. 7 at (4,1) & 7 at (3,0) already counted. 3 at (4,2) and (5,2)? vertical. Check diagonals: (5,1)=4,(4,2)=3 no. So output: add 3 at (2,4),(1,5),(0,6).

Hmm but wait — demo's 7 extension: 7 line direction down-left; extended down-left to edge. Also should extend up-right: (1,5)=0 blocked. Yes.

But is blocking correct? In demo 3 line down-right blocked by 2 at (2,5) — output kept 2. Alternatively extension stops before non-bg. Either way same.

But maybe singles DO extend? In demo, 0 at (1,5) and 2 at (2,5) unchanged. So singles no. Good.

But wait, maybe the rule is about a different geometry: perhaps colors other than the "line colors" (3,7 in demo) are noise. In test colors are 7,3,4. 4 could be noise. Fine.

Also alternative: maybe extension only in one direction (the direction of the line)? 7 line (2,4)→(3,3) direction down-left; extended that way. 3 line (0,3)→(1,4) direction down-right; blocked. Two-direction interpretation gives adding 3s at (0,6),(1,5),(2,4). One-direction gives unchanged grid. Which is more likely? Hmm. In ARC, symmetric extension both ways is common ("extend the line"). But blocking in demo: for the 7 line, extension up-right blocked by 0 at (1,5) — 0 might be background-like? Actually 0 vs bg 5. 0 is a distinct color. Hmm, but maybe rule: lines of length ≥2 extend; singles with... hmm.

Actually wait — reconsider: maybe singles also extend but only if... 0 at (1,5), 2 at (2,5): unchanged, so singles don't extend. OK.

Another thought: maybe the line direction extension is determined by drawing a ray and it passes "through" other colors? In demo, 3 line (0,3),(1,4) continuing down-right hits (2,5)=2: if it overwrote, output (2,5) would be 3 — it's 2. So no.

Let me consider yet another rule: extend each colored diagonal to the grid edge, but stop at any non-bg cell, extending in both directions. I'll go with that.

Actually, let me double check the 7 extension in demo more carefully: 7s at (2,4),(3,3). Output added 7 at (4,2),(5,1),(6,0). Down-left to edge. Up-right: (1,5)=0 blocked. Yes.

Also check demo 0 and 2: could 0 at (1,5),2 at (2,5) be an anti-diagonal of length 2? (1,5),(2,5) vertical. No.

Decision: submit test with added 3s at (0,6),(1,5),(2,4).

Wait — also should the 7 diagonal in test possibly extend up-left? (2,-1) off. Fine.

One more check: could 4 at (5,1) with 3 at (4,2) form something? Different colors, no.

Also, does blocking mean extension stops entirely or skips? Stops. Submit.

Demo analysis: the pattern contains diagonal lines of the same color (length ≥ 2), e.g. the 7s at (2,4),(3,3) — in the output these extend along their diagonal to the grid edge, stopping at any non-background cell (the 3-line down-right was blocked by the 2 at (2,5); the 7-line up-right was blocked by the 0). Single isolated cells stay unchanged.

Applying to the test grid:
- 7 diagonal (3,0),(4,1): up-left is off-grid; down-right next cell (5,2)=3 → blocked.
- 3 diagonal (3,3),(4,2): down-left next (5,1)=4 → blocked; up-right through background: (2,4),(1,5),(0,6) → add 3s.
- Isolated 4 at (5,1), 3 at (5,2): unchanged.

Result: add 3 at (0,6), (1,5), (2,4).
